text:
anya (PM): Quick sync — I put together the final acceptance sheet for GA. Need owners/ok for SLA, docs, support, monitoring, pricing. Can folks confirm?

kevin (SRE): Skimmed. Two open infra items: SLO targets for hosted vs dedicated, and oncall escalation for model regressions.

maria (Product): Agreed. Product can accept a slightly looser p99 for very long-context models if SRE + Optimize doc tradeoffs are captured. Need commercial fallback spelled out for Dedicated.

tyler (Sales): From the sales side we need a hard SLA floor for any paying Dedicated commitment. Customers expect 99.9% availability + clear credit formula. We can be flexible on latency tiers if priced.

jess (Docs): I'll own the public readiness guide + runbooks. Need exact escalation steps & playbook snippets from SRE. ETA end of week if owners confirmed.

kevin (SRE): Proposed SLOs (for review):
```yaml
hosted:
  availability: 99.95%
  latency_p99: <=300ms (single-turn text gen typical)
dedicated:
  availability: 99.9%
  latency_p99: <=500ms (depends on model/quantization)
private:
  availability: contractual
  latency: best-effort, monitored
```
We also need error budget policy and automatic fallback to smaller model variant when error budget exceeds X%.

anya (PM): That looks reasonable as a starting point. Who owns the credit calc and communication?

tyler (Sales): I can draft the commercial credit language but need legal signoff. Also want a priced escalation lane: +SLA for +$X/month per reserved GPU.

maria (Product): We should avoid new pricing lanes close to GA launch. Can we gate premium SLA as "available post-GA" unless enterprise pilot signups exist?

kevin (SRE): For oncall, propose:
1) model-regression alert -> primary SRE paging (severity cat 2)
2) if model quality degrades across >5% of eval traffic -> product + data science followup (severity cat 1 after 30m)
3) auto-fallback route to smaller/safer model variant + traffic steering policy
I'll drop the exact alert thresholds into the ops playbook.

ops-bot: Reminder — runbook templates available at https://intra.redwood/runbooks (use template "model-regression")

jess (Docs): Will embed the SRE steps and paste the alert examples. Example snippet I need from SRE: the actual Alert rule (promql OR log pattern).

kevin (SRE): Example alert (placeholder):
```promql
sum(rate(model_response_error_total[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(model_requests_total[5m])) by (model) > 0.05
```
We can refine thresholds after pilot.

anya (PM): Ok action items:
- kevin: finalize SLO doc + alert rules (owner) — due Thu EOD (1788975600)
- jess: publish GA readiness guide + runbook draft — due Fri (1789062000)
- tyler: draft commercial credit language & pricing lane proposal — due Mon (1789148400)
- maria: decision on premium SLA gating (post-GA vs pilot) — due Mon (1789148400)
- sre-oncall: confirm paging rota + rotation handoff doc — due Thu (1788975600)

kevin (SRE): I'll also add an automated fallback policy to the routing layer: when error budget > 50% burned in 1h, steer tiered traffic to reserve pool.

maria (Product): For launch criteria, product accepts GA if: docs published, oncall rota staffed, basic SLOs in place, and pricing page has provisional tiers + footnote about Dedicated/Private. Non-blocking: premium SLA lane.

tyler (Sales): Fine. Need a single line we can give Enterprise customers if they ask today: "We offer Dedicated with contractual SLA; enterprise pricing & premium SLAs by negotiation." That is enough.

anya (PM): Great — I'll update the acceptance sheet and ping legal. Jess — once you have runbook draft, send to #eng-oncall for review.

jess (Docs): Will do.

sre-oncall: rota confirmed for GA week. Can take primary paging.

anya (PM): Final ask — please add any unresolved blockers to the doc: https://intra.redwood/ga-acceptance-sheet (I added a "must-resolve" flag). If no major objections by EOD Thu we'll mark this as "GA-ready" and schedule the greenlight readout. :white_check_mark:

kevin (SRE): ack.

maria (Product): ack.

tyler (Sales): ack.

jess (Docs): ack.

sre-oncall: ack.
